correctness.rationale: PASS. Quasi-total Roman means every zero sees a 2, and every 2 has some positive neighbor (isolated positive vertices are allowed only with label 1). In Cr_n, if a shore lacks 2, the opposite shore is wholly positive; such a configuration has weight≥n+2, with equality at n4 impossible because the required single supportive opposite-shore vertex is the unique missing matched neighbor. Thus any candidate ≤6 has 2 in each shore. With at least three 2 labels weight6 would contain no 1 and the unique 2 on a shore has no positive neighbor outside its matched forced partner. Therefore exactly one 2 and one 1 on each shore. If 2s are matched at index i, supporting 1s can be independently chosen at j,l≠i giving n(n−1)^2; if 2s are at different indices i,k, matched zero prohibition forces 1 at a_k and b_i, giving n(n−1). Every listed function feasible, so gamma=6 and n²(n−1) minima for n≥4. Independent bounded-weight complete enumeration through n7 agrees counts 48,100,180,294 and n3 exceptional count37. The universal proof is combinatorial rather than extrapolation.
residual_risks: Minimum level only; does not enumerate higher-weight quasi-total Roman functions.
Finite verifier calculations corroborate rather than replace all-orders proofs.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS. Cabrera-García et al. arXiv:1903.09789 provide the precise quasi-total Roman definition and general inequalities, cycles and boundary conditions, but inspection of the 15-page full paper finds no crown or complete-bipartite optimizer classification. A prior exact all-function theorem for complete multipartite graphs yields gamma_qtR(K_nn)=4, but a crown deletes one matched edge at each vertex, invalidating those optima. A 2022 quasi-total Roman bondage paper studies edge deletion and hardness; no inspected material implies this matching-deleted sharp count. No equivalent crown result found by crown/Knn−M/alias Resultary searches; unindexed aliases remain a risk.
residual_risks: Differently phrased crown QTR classification in nonindexed older graph-domination literature cannot be excluded.
Statement is n≥4: Cr3=C6 has scalar six but 37 minimum labelings, not n²(n−1).
